corrected_value.title: Genome-wide association studies of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis suggest candidate susceptibility genes
corrected_value.authors: Sharma; Gao; Londono; Devroy; Mauldin; Frankel; Brandon; Zhang; Li; Dobbs; Gurnett; Grant; Hakonarson; Dormans; Herring; Gordon; Wise

decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding (target 0) identify Sharma et al. (2011) [15] (DOI: 10.1093/hmg/ddq571) as the tested original study. The primary text explicitly states that the present study was conducted to validate the association of SNP rs10510181 with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) reported by Sharma et al. [15]. Other cited genetic studies (e.g., references 6-14 for other loci and reference 18 for CHL1 tag SNP intervals in schizophrenia) are cited solely as background or for tag SNP selection, not re-tested.

decisions.quote:
Recently, Sharma et al. [
15
] reported the association between SNP rs10510181, in the proximity of the CHL1 gene, and AIS by performing GWAS in 419 Caucasian families with AIS. The present study was conducted to validate the association of SNP rs10510181 with AIS. The results showed that rs10510181 was not associated with AIS in a Han Chinese population. Furthermore, 4 SNPs covering the entire region of the CHL1 gene were not associated with the occurrence of AIS either, indicating that the CHL1 gene might not be associated with AIS.
The previously reported association of rs10510181 with AIS predisposition in Caucasians was not replicated in our study.
decisions.reason: Although initial Stage I screening (186 cases, 169 controls) showed a putative allelic difference for rs10510181, enlarging the sample in Stage II to the full powered cohort (500 cases, 500 controls) showed no significant genotype (P = 0.39) or allelic (P = 0.30) association, nor any association across four additional CHL1 SNPs. Following Codebook Step 3 Rule 1, the authors state an explicit overall failure verdict: 'The previously reported association of rs10510181 with AIS predisposition in Caucasians was not replicated in our study.'

decisions.quote:
A previous genome-wide association study (GWAS) suggested a strong association between the single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs10510181 in the proximity of the gene encoding a cell adhesion molecule with homology to L1CAM (CHL1) and adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) in Caucasians. To clarify the role of
CHL1
in the etiopathogenesis of AIS, we performed a case-control replication study in a Han Chinese population.
decisions.reason: The study collected new genetic data from an independent sample of 500 female Han Chinese AIS patients and 500 age- and sex-matched controls to re-test the published association between SNP rs10510181 near CHL1 and AIS reported by Sharma et al. (2011), making it a replication.
